Definition: probably from an obsolete διάκω (to run on errands; compare G1377); an attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a deacon or deaconess):--deacon, minister, servant.
BiblicalUsage: A servant is one who waits at table, and in the New Testament the word grows into deacon, minister, and servant of Christ. Phoebe is called a servant of the church at Cenchrea, Paul greets the deacons at Philippi and sets out how a deacon must live, and Jesus says whoever would be great among His people must be their minister.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title servant is the highest honour the church gives. Christ took the towel and the basin, and every deacon and minister since stands in that line, serving the table and the people of God.
